description: Gaius Octavius, later known as Augustus created a series of laws between 30 BCE and 2 BCE that transformed the constitution of the Roman Republic into the Constitution of the Roman Empire.  One of which created a standing army of approximately 28 legions consisting of 5,000-6,000 professional soldiers.
tooltip: Reorganizes the Roman army into a professional standing force. Existing Roman-employed Cretan Archer and Balearic Slinger mercenaries are converted into terminal Auxiliary troops; Allied Italian Horse Javelineers are replaced by Numidian Auxiliary Horse Javelineers. The reformed Market recruits Auxiliaries instead of mercenaries. Unlocks the reformed Roman military roster, including Centurions and Onagers.
